message.content:
`contenteditable` accepts three distinct string values: | Value | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `"true"` | The element is editable. | | `"false"` | The element is not editable. | | `"plaintext-only"` | The element is editable, but only plain text can be entered (no formatting). | So when you’re given the value **`"plaintext-only"`**, you should use that exact string as the attribute value. It is already a valid value for `contenteditable`; there’s no need (and no way) to convert it to a boolean string like `"true"` or `"false"` because it represents a different mode of editability. **Example** ```html
This text can be edited, but only as plain text.
``` If you’re working programmatically and need to validate that a supplied value is one of the allowed options, you can simply check against the set `{ "true", "false", "plaintext-only" }`. No conversion is required.
